_README: Static reference table: NFL stadium name (as it appears verbatim in
data/raw/*/schedules.parquet's `stadium` column) -> elevation above sea
level in meters/feet. Built 2026-08-21 for the altitude-adaptation screen
(scripts/altitude_screen.py). No stadium elevation table existed in this
repo before (verified absent by grep over docs/, registry/, scripts/,
Provenance per entry (AGENTS.md label rule):
inferred=false -> documented venue figure (Denver's three names: the
5,280 ft 'Mile High' figure; Azteca: Wikipedia infobox 2,241 m,
inferred=true -> REPORTED general knowledge, approximate: city/area
terrain elevation from Wikipedia stadium/city articles and map
familiarity, NOT surveyed stadium-site values and NOT fetched live.
Approximation error is tens of meters (~+/-50 m band).
Keyed by exact `stadium` string (not `stadium_id`, which is unreliable
for neutral-site games -- see docs/travel_rest_battery.md). Renamed
stadiums at the same physical site get separate entries with identical
elevations -- simple and correct, slightly redundant.
Covers every distinct `stadium` name appearing in REG games 2009-2025
(49 names, enumerated from data/raw/20260817T235649Z/schedules.parquet;
0 unresolved names in the scored window).
Threshold note frozen before scoring (docs/altitude_screen.md): the
4,000-ft visitor-deficit threshold versus Denver classifies Glendale AZ
(~355 m, deficit ~4,114 ft) as IN and Las Vegas (~610 m, ~3,277 ft) as
OUT; Glendale sits within one approximation-error band of the line and
this is disclosed rather than tuned.
